title: When two agents talk, who is a person and who is an AI?
checkedAgainst: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0 (in progress; as published on 2026-11-13), section 8, read and not run: `model.test.ts` holds the model to the rules and examples of 8.1 to 8.13, each test naming its section, and `answers.ts` computes the answers below from the model. There is no reference implementation here to run the model against. It is also held to what the protocol itself publishes, copied on 2026-11-13 into `fixtures/poppy-official.json`: the model accepts every example message and ID of spec.md's section 8, rejects every message the Company kit's message schema rejects, and writes state and authorization events that pass its event schema.

grounding.subject: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0, as published on 2026-11-13
grounding.label: Read, not run: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0, as published on 2026-11-13
grounding.sentence: Checked by reading, not running: the Personal Agent Protocol draft 1.0, as published on 2026-11-13.

answer: Every message says whether a person or an AI wrote it, on both sides, and only your own agent can bring you in

questions.question: Your agent tells Alex in its own words that you want a medium. Then you type "Medium, please." yourself. What author.type does each message carry, and what role?
questions.answer: The agent’s summary is agent and your own words are human. Both have role user: role says which side, author.type says person or AI.

questions.question: While the Direct Conversation is open, your agent sends a message of its own to the first conversation. What comes back, and when will that conversation take it?
questions.answer: 409 direct_conversation_open: the first conversation waits while the Direct Conversation is open, and takes messages again once it closes.

questions.question: The Company wants to talk with you, not your agent. What can it do, and who opens the Direct Conversation?
questions.answer: It adds a user_requested event, which changes no state field. Only your agent opens a Direct Conversation, after asking you, so you decide when you are brought in.

questions.question: The conversation has used your account A. What does the Company answer if your agent sends a message signed out, if another User ID uses the same Conversation ID, and if your agent signed in to account B tries?
questions.answer: Signed out: 401 with a challenge to sign in again. Another User ID: 404 conversation_not_found. Account B: 404 conversation_not_found, the same answer as for an ID that does not exist.

questions.question: Your agent has sent a message and working is still true. Why should it read before it closes the conversation?
questions.answer: A close does not wait its turn, so the Company may drop the message it has not acted on yet. Reading until working is false makes sure it was handled first.

steps.title: Your agent opens a conversation
steps.line: Predict: where will the shop’s reply come from?
steps.caption: Your agent wants to exchange the jacket from order 1042, so it talks with example.com’s own agent: JSON over HTTPS, signed with its Session header as chapter 1 showed. Its first message starts the conversation. The answer is 201 with a Conversation ID, cnv_8f3Kd2, and no reply: the Company has accepted the message, not answered it, so working is true. Where will the reply come from?
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your agent and you sit on your side; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and an empty seat for a person. Its fields: working true, handoff none, responder agent, closed false. No Direct Conversation has opened. On the conversation’s table, your agent says “Return jacket 1042.”, marked AI (author.type agent, role user). The rule, from section 8.3 of the draft: Accepted is not answered: the agent reads until working is false.

steps.title: Replies are read, not returned
steps.caption: The agent reads the conversation’s events from where it last stopped, or holds the read open, or streams it. The reply is an event, and it says who wrote it: here an AI. Every message says whether a person or an AI wrote it, on both sides, and only your own agent can bring you in. A request lost on the way is safe to send again with the same request ID: the Company acts on it once.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your agent and you sit on your side; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and an empty seat for a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder agent, closed false. No Direct Conversation has opened. On the conversation’s table, the Company Agent says “Insulated: $70 more?”, marked AI (author.type agent, role company). The rule, from section 8.8 of the draft: Every message says whether a person or an AI wrote it.

steps.title: A person takes the empty seat
steps.line: Pending, then a person joins: responder is human.
steps.caption: The agent asks for a person. Handoff turns pending while the Company looks, and its agent keeps answering meanwhile, so responder stays agent. When Alex joins, handoff is none again, responder is human, and Alex’s reply carries the person mark. Had nobody been free, handoff would go back to none and the Company Agent would say why. A cancel may not take effect, so the agent watches these fields.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your agent and you sit on your side; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. No Direct Conversation has opened. On the conversation’s table, Alex says “Which size?”, marked person (author.type human, role company). The rule, from section 8.7 of the draft: A person at the Company wrote this: its author.type is human.

steps.title: The Company asks for you
steps.line: Predict: can the Company bring you in itself?
steps.caption: Alex wants to confirm the exchange with you, not with your agent. The Company cannot reach you. It can only add a user_requested event to the conversation, with a short reason, and none of the four fields changes. The invitation lands in front of your agent, which asks you whether you want to talk. What happens if you say no?
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your agent and you sit on your side; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. No Direct Conversation has opened. The Company’s invitation, a user_requested envelope, lies in front of your agent, waiting for your answer. On the conversation’s table, Alex says “Which size?”, marked person (author.type human, role company). The rule, from section 8.10 of the draft: The Company asks for you, and only your agent can bring you in.

steps.title: A second, smaller table
steps.line: Only your agent can open it.
steps.caption: You agree, so your agent opens a Direct Conversation: a new conversation, linked to the first, where you speak for yourself and your agent may watch. The Company keeps the earlier history, and you need not read it. Had you said no, your agent would have told the Company for you. While the small table is open, the first one waits: a message there gets 409 direct_conversation_open.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your seat is empty and your agent has stepped away to watch; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. It is paused. A Direct Conversation is open at a smaller table below: you sit at it, your agent watches from beside it, and across from you sits a specialist, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. On the Direct Conversation’s table, the specialist says “Which size?”, marked person (author.type human, role company). The rule, from section 8.10 of the draft: A Direct Conversation is linked to the first, which waits; your agent may observe.

steps.title: Your own words are marked human
steps.line: The same words from your agent would be marked AI.
steps.caption: You type “Medium, please.” and your agent sends it as written, marked human. Had your agent passed on your wish in its own words, as a summary, the message would be marked agent: only your own words count as yours. The specialist’s reply carries the person mark too, so all four voices stay distinct. Draft 1.0 adds that either side reads a mark it does not know as AI, so nothing passes for a person’s words unless it says human.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your seat is empty and your agent has stepped away to watch; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. It is paused. A Direct Conversation is open at a smaller table below: you sit at it, your agent watches from beside it, and across from you sits a specialist, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. On the Direct Conversation’s table, the specialist says “Done: medium.”, marked person (author.type human, role company). The rule, from section 8.10 of the draft: A Direct Conversation is linked to the first, which waits; your agent may observe.

steps.title: Who may continue this conversation
steps.line: A mismatch looks like no conversation at all.
steps.caption: Suppose the Company Agent had needed your account. It adds an authorization event; your agent signs you in and carries on in the same conversation with an access token. From then on the conversation belongs to agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK and account A, whatever Session asks. Signed out, the agent gets a challenge to sign in again. Another User ID, or account B, gets 404, as if it did not exist.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your seat is empty and your agent has stepped away to watch; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. It is paused. A Direct Conversation is open at a smaller table below: you sit at it, your agent watches from beside it, and across from you sits a specialist, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. On the Direct Conversation’s table, the specialist says “Done: medium.”, marked person (author.type human, role company). A place card names the conversation’s owner: agent.example, User ID usr_Q7c1vK, account A. A message from that owner signed in to account A is accepted; signed out: 401; another user: 404; account B: 404. The rule, from section 8.10 of the draft: A Direct Conversation is linked to the first, which waits; your agent may observe.

steps.title: The small table closes, the big one listens
steps.line: Now drive both sides yourself: refusals say why.
steps.caption: You are done, so your agent closes the Direct Conversation, and the first conversation takes messages again. A close does not wait its turn: the Company may drop anything it has not acted on yet, so the agent reads until working is false before it closes. Closing does not cancel the exchange itself. Now press the events, for both sides, and read why a refused press is refused.
steps.picture: At the conversation’s table (cnv_8f3Kd2), your agent and you sit on your side; on the Company’s side sit the Company Agent and Alex, a person. Its fields: working false, handoff none, responder human, closed false. A Direct Conversation was opened and has closed. Nothing is said on the table in use. The rule, from section 8.10 of the draft: The Direct Conversation has closed, so the conversation takes messages again.
